text.p: Merrill Lynch said Monday it had downgraded Panamerican Beverages Inc (Panamco) to neutral from accumulate.
"We believe that the recently announced acquisition in Venezuela is likely to be dilutive to Panamco's shareholders," analysts Enrique Figueroa and Alicia Frank wrote in a report.
They said they estimate net revenues from the purchase of $460-480 million for 1997.
They said a challenge for the company will be continuing weak demand in Brazil, Panamco's most important market, and competition from Pepsi brands.
"The required profitability for the operation to avoid dilution is very high," the analysts wrote.
They added that the Coca-Cola bottler's stock had practically reached the brokerage's price objective of $30-$31.
Panamco's shares stood at 28-7/8 in early trading.
